title: An inflationary gap in Rivon with no policy response
scenario: Rivon is an invented country whose real GDP is above full-employment output, and its government takes no policy action.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a correctly labeled AD-AS graph showing Rivon's current short-run equilibrium, with LRAS, and show the long-run adjustment and the new long-run equilibrium.

rubric.point: Correctly labeled graph: Price level and Real GDP on the axes, AD, SRAS and a vertical LRAS, with the current output to the right of full-employment output
accept: PL and Y (or real output) as axis labels

rubric.point: New long-run equilibrium on LRAS at full-employment output, with a higher price level than the current one

parts.sample: The graph has Price level on the vertical axis and Real GDP on the horizontal axis. AD1 and SRAS1 cross at PL1 and Y1, to the right of the vertical LRAS at YF. SRAS1 shifts left to SRAS2, which crosses AD1 on LRAS at YF and a higher price level PL2.

key.because: a rise in nominal wages and input prices

slips.AD: With no policy, spending does not change. The economy adjusts through nominal wages and input prices, which shift SRAS.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain why the curve you shifted in part A shifts in the long run.

rubric.point: Unemployment is below the natural rate (labor is scarce), so nominal wages and input prices rise, raising firms' costs
accept: workers are scarce, so wages are bid up as contracts are renewed

parts.sample: Because output is above full employment, unemployment is below the natural rate and firms compete for scarce workers. As contracts are renewed, nominal wages and other input prices rise, which raises production costs and shifts SRAS to the left.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Compared with today, identify what happens to Rivon's unemployment rate once the economy is back in long-run equilibrium.

rubric.point: It rises, to the natural rate of unemployment
accept: it increases back to the natural rate

parts.sample: The unemployment rate rises, back up to the natural rate of unemployment, because output falls back to full-employment output.
